about: Whether an owner identity owns an Identity Agent, decided from their two key logs (ADR-087). Each case gives the Identity Agent's log, the owner's log, where the verifier took each copy from, any other copy or log it holds, and the grade and reason code the check must give. The rules are in contracts/owned/owned.md. Every key comes from a seed published here.

cases.label: owned-and-anchored
cases.why: The owner's log seals the Identity Agent's inception in an interaction event. Both copies came from the party being checked, so the proof is anchored and no more.

cases.label: owned-and-confirmed
cases.why: The same two logs, each taken from its own witnesses, with the inception and the anchoring interaction receipted to the threshold each log names.

cases.label: confirmed-is-never-reported-for-a-copy-the-checked-party-handed-over
cases.why: Every receipt is present and the Identity Agent's log came from its witnesses, but the owner's log was handed over by the party being checked, which can hide a later event.

cases.label: anchoring-event-not-receipted
cases.why: Both logs came from their witnesses, but the anchoring interaction carries no receipt, so the owner's witness is not shown to have seen it.

cases.label: look-alike-names-the-owner
cases.why: Somebody else founded an Identity Agent whose inception names the same owner identity. Its log verifies and names the owner, and the owner's log seals a different inception: named, not owned.

cases.label: delegation-approval-offered-as-an-anchor
cases.why: The owner's interaction seals the inception of an identity it delegated: the same seal shape as an anchor. What is sealed is a delegated inception, which is never owned.

cases.label: machine-log-begins-with-a-delegated-inception
cases.why: The log begins with a delegated inception that also carries an owner seal naming the owner, and the owner's log seals it. It is named, and a log that begins with a delegated inception can never be owned.

cases.label: anchor-in-an-establishment-event
cases.why: The seal of the Identity Agent's inception is in a rotation of the owner identity. An anchor is read only from an interaction event, because an event seal in an establishment event is that identity's own owner seal.

cases.label: old-copy-hides-a-removal
cases.why: The owner identity has since replaced the anchoring interaction by a recovery rotation, and the party being checked hands over the old copy. It still verifies, so it proves anchored and can prove no more: only the owner's witnesses can show the removal.

cases.label: old-copy-against-a-copy-the-verifier-kept
cases.why: The same old copy, shown to a verifier that already holds the owner's log with the recovery rotation in it. The copy does not carry on from the one kept, so it is refused.

cases.label: anchor-removed-by-a-recovery-rotation
cases.why: The owner's log now holds a recovery rotation where the anchoring interaction was, and the verifier kept the earlier copy, so it can say the anchor was removed and has not been made again.

cases.label: anchored-again-after-a-recovery
cases.why: After the recovery rotation the owner anchors the same inception in a new interaction event, which stands.

cases.label: owner-left-and-came-back
cases.why: The owner was named at the inception, left out by the first rotation and named again by the second. Its anchor of the inception no longer counts: it is owned only from the event where it came back, which nothing anchors yet.

cases.label: owner-came-back-and-anchored-the-event
cases.why: The same Identity Agent, once the owner has anchored the rotation in which it came back.

cases.label: owner-left
cases.why: A later rotation of the Identity Agent names another owner alone. The old anchor stays in the owner's log and means only that it agreed at that event.

cases.label: second-machine-anchored-in-one-owner-log
cases.why: The owner's log anchors one Identity Agent and later a second. The first anchored is the only one this owner identity can own: the second is named, not owned.

cases.label: first-machine-in-an-owner-log-that-anchors-two
cases.why: The same owner log, checked for the Identity Agent it anchored first, which it still owns.

cases.label: seal-names-an-identifier-whose-log-was-not-supplied
cases.why: Before the anchor, the owner's log seals an event of another identifier, and the verifier was not given that identifier's log. Whether that was an earlier anchor cannot be told, so the result is that the log could not be checked.

cases.label: duplicitous-owner-log
cases.why: The verifier holds a second, validly signed interaction event at the place of the anchoring one. Two events at one place that no recovery explains are duplicity, and no Identity Agent is owned by such an owner.
